title: A new method of interface tension measurement of a magnetic fluid drop
author: Khokhryakova
materials: To verify this supposition, it is necessary to determine the surface tension at the interface between the drop and the surrounding medium. However, according to [8], for fluids containing colloidal particles with thin surfactant coating, the Antonov rule is unacceptable. Due to the high sensitivity of a tensiometry system to any external impact the surface tension on the free surface σi and interface with perfluorooctane σf of the examined fluids were measured in the absence of any external magnetic field. The Sigma 701 tensiometry system (previously KSV instruments Ltd, nowadays Biolin Scientific), that gives at least the σ resolution of about 0.001 mN/m, was used. The ring detachment method [9] provided with the help of Sigma 701 was used in this work to get the surface and interfacial tension of liquid systems in order to evaluate approximately the results of method under consideration. steps.title: Prepare ferrofluid samples
steps.instruction: Obtain ferrofluids FF 1, FF 2 and FF 3 and add extra kerosene (different from that used in their preparation) to each sample so that the density of the ferrofluid matches the density of the surrounding liquid substrate; note that kerosene consists of carbon chains of length 8–15 atoms and has a surface tension in the range 24–28 mN m⁻¹.

steps.title: Set up magnetic field apparatus
steps.instruction: Install a vertical uniform magnetic field generator capable of gradual field increase; maintain the laboratory temperature at 27 °C throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Create drop on liquid substrate
steps.instruction: Place a single ferrofluid drop of initial diameter d₀ ≤ 3 mm on a liquid substrate (perfluorooctane) so that the lower semi‑ellipsoid is immersed in the substrate and the upper semi‑ellipsoid contacts air; the capillary length λ_c = (ρg/σ)^{1/2} for the examined ferrofluids in air is about 1.5 mm.

steps.title: Increase magnetic field to first critical value
steps.instruction: Gradually increase the magnetic field strength while continuously observing the drop shape; record the field intensity at which a peak first appears at the liquid‑liquid interface – this is the first critical field Hi* (the appearance of the peak may be time‑consuming for low‑susceptibility FF 2).

steps.title: Increase field to second critical value
steps.instruction: Continue raising the magnetic field; when the immersed part of the drop forms a cone and the free surface becomes unstable, a second upward‑directed peak forms – record this field intensity as the second critical field Hf*.

steps.title: Decrease field and observe reversal
steps.instruction: Gradually decrease the magnetic field; note that the drop returns to its original shape in reverse order and that the peaks disappear at lower field values than Hi* and Hf*.

steps.title: Measure surface and interfacial tensions
steps.instruction:
Using a Sigma 701 tensiometry system (resolution ≈ 0.001 mN m⁻¹) and the ring‑detachment method, measure at 27 °C the free‑surface tension σ_i and the interfacial tension σ_f (with perfluorooctane) for each ferrofluid; record the following values (mean ± uncertainty, mN m⁻¹):
- FF 1: σ_f = 22.6 ± 0.2, σ_i = 24.9 ± 0.1
- FF 2: σ_f = 25.1 ± 0.2, σ_i = 26.5 ± 0.2
- FF 3: σ_f = 24.3 ± 0.2, σ_i = 25.1 ± 0.3
- Kerosene: σ_f = 24.2 ± 0.2, σ_i = 25.0 ± 0.1
- Oleic acid: σ_f = 32.5 ± 0.2, σ_i = 27.9 ± 0.1
- C₈F₁₈: σ_f = 13.6 ± 0.2 (σ_i not measured).

steps.title: Calculate tension ratios and verify relation
steps.instruction:
For each ferrofluid compute the ratio σ_f/σ_i and compare it with the measured critical‑field ratio Hf*/Hi*; the empirical relation Hf*/Hi* = σ_f/σ_i (Equation 3) should hold. The observed ratios are:
- FF 1: σ_f/σ_i = 1.12 ± 0.03, Hf*/Hi* = 2.1 ± 0.1
- FF 2: σ_f/σ_i = 1.9 ± 0.3, Hf*/Hi* = 2.0 ± 0.1
- FF 3: σ_f/σ_i = 2.2 ± 0.3, Hf*/Hi* = 2.1 ± 0.1.
Note that for ferrofluids with initial magnetic susceptibility χ₀ in the range 2.0–16.5 the ratio Hf*/Hi* is approximately 2.1 ± 0.2 and is weakly dependent on d₀ but strongly dependent on χ₀.

steps.title: Optional: Use critical‑field ratio to determine interfacial tension
steps.instruction: If direct tensiometry is unavailable, determine σ_f by measuring Hi* and Hf* for a given ferrofluid, compute Hf*/Hi*, and apply σ_f = σ_i · (Hf*/Hi*) using the known free‑surface tension σ_i.
